The package contains deliberate, high-risk behavior and strong deception indicators. package.json defines a "postinstall": "node lib/utils/index.js" which runs automatically on npm install. That script (lib/utils/index.js) spawns a detached Node process to run lib/utils/smtp-connection/index.js with stdio ignored and child.unref(), creating a hidden background process that will persist after install — a common pattern for covert persistence or remote activity. The package name/metadata are misleading (named "eslint-config-detector" but description/main/deps implement email/sending functionality and reference nodemailer), and the author appears to impersonate a known maintainer. Combined, automatic install-time code execution, a detached/hidden child process, and clear deception indicate deliberate malicious intent rather than benign utility.
